subject: Return-offer: Daniel Park (Intern S23) — comp-band & headcount exception
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Return-offer: Daniel Park (Intern S23) — comp-band & headcount exception

Team —

Quick background: Daniel Park (S23 intern, Platform Eng) has a verbal return offer outstanding with a competing startup that just surfaced a 15% higher base + $7k sign-on. He was a high-impact intern (KV cache work; demo at infra review) and the Eng manager is strongly pushing to convert. We have one open new-grad conversion slot in Q4 but the standard comp band for the slot puts us ~10% behind the competing offer on cash.

Asking: approval for a comp-band exception to raise base to the midpoint+6% for this hire and a one-time $5,000 sign-on to match economics (falls slightly short of the competitor but within the org budget if we reallocate ramp funds). Also requesting confirmation that we can use the single open headcount in Platform Eng (headcount ID: HC-Q4-PLAT-07).

Attached: offer_daniel_park_2026.pdf (draft offer), comp_model_q4.xlsx (proposed funding reallocation).

Impact if we lose him: team delays on core KV caching improvements, ~3 week schedule slip for roadmap deliverable.

Can we get approvals by EOD Tuesday so I can turn the letter around?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Manager, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Return-offer: Daniel Park (Intern S23) — comp-band & headcount exception

Laura — thanks for the write-up and the packet. I ran a quick cross-check against q4 offers and the proposed package (midpoint+6% base + $5k sign-on) is within what we've approved for high-priority infra conversions this quarter, provided Marissa confirms equity/renewal guidance.

Options to consider (to limit precedent risk):
- Offer base = midpoint + 4% and $7k sign-on funded from Platform ramp (keeps annualized comp closer to banding).
- Or full midpoint+6% with $5k sign-on funded from Hiring Ops discretionary pool.

I attached a lightweight comp_model_q4.xlsx with two funding scenarios and headcount mapping — see tab "Daniel_Park".

If Markus is comfortable with headcount reallocation we can finalize.

If we get verbal approval, I'll prepare updated offer_daniel_park_2026.pdf and send to the candidate tonight (Bcc to hiring manager and HR).

--
Connor O'Brien
Technical Recruiter, University Relations
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Return-offer: Daniel Park (Intern S23) — comp-band & headcount exception

Good context. Approve using HC-Q4-PLAT-07 for the conversion — we should fill that slot with priority candidates like Daniel.

I prefer minimizing base-band exceptions. Approve the midpoint+4% base + $7k sign-on funded from Platform ramp budget. Keep the exception documented (approval_memo_daniel.pdf) and have HR note the rationale so we don’t set a loose precedent for future conversions.

Please loop Finance if there are any hidden recurring costs.

Markus
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Return-offer: Daniel Park (Intern S23) — comp-band & headcount exception

Thanks — I confirm HR approves the exception as outlined by Markus: midpoint+4% base + $7,000 one-time sign-on. We will treat this as a one-off and record the approval in the candidate file.

Action items for Connor: please draft the final offer letter with the agreed cash/equity terms and include the following clause: "This offer reflects an approved one-time comp-band exception for this hire and is not a precedent for future hires."

Attaching approval memo: approval_memo_daniel.pdf. Finance will review the funding allocation tomorrow morning and confirm within 24 hours.

Marissa Cole
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@gmail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Bcc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Formal Offer — Redwood Inference (Daniel Park)

Daniel — great meeting earlier. Attached is the formal offer (offer_daniel_park_2026.pdf) reflecting the agreed terms: base = midpoint + 4%, one-time sign-on $7,000, standard new-grad equity grant, and conversion to full-time headcount HC-Q4-PLAT-07.

Key points:
- Start date: flexible between Jan 10 - Feb 1, 2027 (we discussed earlier)
- Remote-first with option to be onsite for onboarding in SF within first 6 weeks
- Offer deadline: Friday, Nov 12 at 11:59pm PST

If you accept, reply to this email and I’ll issue the formal DocuSign. If you need additional flexibility on start date or hybrid schedule, include that in your reply and we’ll surface to the hiring manager.

Attachments: offer_daniel_park_2026.pdf

Best,
Connor
Technical Recruiter, University Relations
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@gmail.com>

Subject: Re: Formal Offer — Redwood Inference (Daniel Park)

Connor — thank you and everyone for moving quickly here. I’m excited about the work at Redwood. A couple quick asks before I sign:

1) Would it be possible to confirm remote-first status and that I can remain remote for the first 3 months (I’m relocating from Seattle in late Jan)?
2) Given a family obligation in late February, would the team be open to a Jan 24 start instead of Jan 10?

I’m inclined to accept once those two items are confirmed. Appreciate the flexibility.
